svg.aria-label: The Cb Cr chroma plane at three luma levels
svg.text: The Cb/Cr plane: where color lives once brightness is removed
Y' says how bright. Cb and Cr say only which hue and how saturated. Neutral grey is always the exact centre.
Horizontal: Cb, from -0.5 (yellow) to +0.5 (blue). Vertical: Cr, from +0.5 (red) at the top to -0.5 (cyan).
Rings on the middle panel mark where the six pure RGB corners land - they sit on the boundary, at maximum saturation.
Why this matters: neighbouring pixels usually share almost the same Cb/Cr even where Y' changes fast. That redundancy is what 4:2:0 spends.
It is also why chroma keying, skin-tone gates and 'is this pitch or is this a shirt?' masks are easier here than in RGB.
